findings.title: The texture layout was not linear
findings.found: The first full-width texture interpretation was wrong. Recovered upload traversal established tiled storage instead.
findings.why: A file can pass size checks while its pixels are decoded in the wrong order. The decoder was corrected.
findings.unknown: These are custom repacked structures, not ordinary TIM files or universal texture coverage.

findings.title: The pose packing is mapped
findings.found: Bit-origin reconstruction recovered sparse axes and an overlapping-store effect in one packed pose helper.
findings.why: There is a testable mapping behind the pose decoder, not just a plausible-looking model.
findings.unknown: A fixed-block check, not a complete animation system or provenance clearance.

findings.title: Sequence calls are not frames
findings.found: The primary updater was checked against a separate oracle. A zero duration expires after 256 update calls.
findings.why: A repeating hold is not an end signal. Assuming a frame rate would change the animation semantics.
findings.unknown: 55 nonempty sequences are exposed; timing and a complete animation system are not established.

findings.title: Geometry is real; gameplay is not
findings.found: A bounded environment decoder matched 863 reference rows, retaining coordinates, UVs, flags and material evidence.
findings.why: The scene has structured reconstruction evidence beyond an isolated visual guess.
findings.unknown: Visibility, broader orientations, collision and material semantics remain incomplete.

findings.title: A character is more than loose parts
findings.found: Recovered hierarchy and part mapping support a diagnostic character with 317 vertices and 316 faces.
findings.why: Part identities connect to a skeleton; duplicate render packets were workspaces, not extra faces.
findings.unknown: Transforms are approximate. Full animation and original GPU/GTE fidelity are not established.

findings.title: The first inspected map is not boot
findings.found: The zero-state startup path resolves to ST01. Its established direct order is INIT_DAT → DEMO_DAT → ST01.
findings.why: The earlier ST1C environment cannot be substituted for the first startup scene or called a title screen.
findings.unknown: This is not the complete dependency set, an executed native scene or a boot result.

findings.title: Native policy is not BIOS equivalence
findings.found: Selected A0:39 analysis reports five ordered word stores. The accepted native heap policy deliberately preserves guest RAM.
findings.why: A passing native-policy test does not prove the original firmware performed the same effects.
findings.unknown: Actual game-time dispatch, allocator invariants and inherited GPU state remain unresolved.

findings.title: Observe without inventing a step
findings.found: A four-case envelope captured bounded owner state, including the actual pending A0:49 request.
findings.why: Inspection can report where execution stopped without pretending the pending service completed.
findings.unknown: Fingerprints are not full-state introspection. No Windows capture or live-debugger acceptance.

findings.title: Old data is allowed to look old
findings.found: Delayed wakes recover sampled data; failed observations retain explicit stale/as-of labels without replaying requests.
findings.why: An old snapshot must never silently masquerade as current runtime state.
findings.unknown: Mode repetitions are not unique tests. No timing guarantee, LeakSanitizer pass or native-owner retirement.

findings.title: The original reached a gameplay scene
findings.found: A bounded original-game controller capture progressed through New Game to a corridor with the gameplay HUD; its selected helper register chain is complete.
findings.why: The original copy progresses beyond the opening story under documented controller inputs. This is identified emulator research.
findings.unknown: Not native-port boot, isolated movement causality, physical-console proof, complete gameplay or implementation clearance.

findings.title: A0:49 is not a safe no-op
findings.found: Research observed GPU-access callbacks before a context-matched caller return; access payloads remain unknown.
findings.why: Ignoring a return value does not mean the call had no effects. A success constant would invent state.
findings.unknown: Effective dispatch, full ABI, GPU history and current native binding remain open.

findings.title: Cancel requested ≠ work retired
findings.found: New load and host-I/O reviews separate cancellation intent, actual completion, resource settlement and execution retirement.
findings.why: A timeout or an overlapped handle cannot be relabeled as a safe, bounded shutdown.
findings.unknown: No admitted production backend, controller implementation or new Windows test. L1/P1 remain unmet.

items.criterion: Establish bounded tiled texture, mesh, assembled-character and static-environment inspection; this milestone excludes full coverage, production rendering and scene execution.

items.label: Source-bound offline editor foundation
items.criterion: Establish the bounded offline transform-edit/history/sidecar foundation, with portable and frozen synthetic Windows evidence; not a complete current IDE, live apply workflow or pixel acceptance.
items.evidence_class: Reported portable and frozen Windows synthetic evidence

items.label: Native Windows CD startup slice
items.criterion: Accept the bounded mode-00 path using a real same-image reader, FIFO/response/IRQ/callback ownership and reviewed Windows execution, stopping honestly at the unsupported continuation.

items.label: Owned snapshot and portable inspection
items.criterion: Accept bounded actual owner capture and an actual producer-artifact-portable-model round trip; no live controller or Windows GUI display is implied.
items.evidence_class: Actual Linux capture and portable export/import

items.label: Native original-game boot
items.criterion: Accept native Windows startup reaching the required initial game state under an identified authorized run, without a BIOS/emulator runtime dependency.

items.label: Production scene and resource lifecycle
items.criterion: Accept real production scene entry, resource dependencies, visibility/lifetime transitions and teardown, not a static union-geometry view or synthetic first-scene fixture.

items.label: Production renderer fidelity
items.criterion: Accept the required production GPU/GTE, texture/material and rendering semantics against bounded stated references, beyond the approximate CPU diagnostic renderer.

items.label: Complete character animation
items.criterion: Accept integrated pose, animation sequence, transform and timing behavior for the required game use cases; a fixed helper or update-call oracle alone is insufficient.

items.label: Player controls and camera
items.criterion: Demonstrate integrated player input, motion and camera behavior in an accepted native gameplay session.

items.label: Collision and world interaction
items.criterion: Accept required collision, triggers and world-interaction behavior in production scenes, not merely recovered coordinates.

items.label: AI, combat and progression
items.criterion: Accept representative required AI, combat and game-progression behavior in native play, with explicit remaining-coverage limits.

items.label: Decoded audio, music and output
items.criterion: Accept required decoding, music/stream handling and audible native output; nonexecuting sound plans and a CPU mixer checkpoint do not satisfy it.

items.label: Game save/load compatibility
items.criterion: Accept game-state persistence, load/restore and required compatibility; editor sidecars are a different feature.

items.label: Actual-capture Windows viewer
items.criterion: Accept the real standalone launcher, pixel behavior and actual owned-capture GUI display, not synthetic HWND/host-function checks alone.

items.label: Safe live runtime controller
items.criterion: Close necessary production loading, owner-retirement, stop/fault and endpoint lifecycle obligations and accept integrated runtime control; four source reviews alone are insufficient.

items.label: Complete integrated IDE workflow
items.criterion: Accept the intended complete integrated inspection/edit/debug workflow with real runtime interaction, persistence, failures and safe shutdown, not isolated inspection foundations.

items.label: Implementation provenance review
items.criterion: Complete the project-specific independent-implementation provenance review for adopted runtime behavior and references; restricted research remains separate and no legal clean-room certification is implied.

items.label: Native Windows package acceptance
items.criterion: Accept the authorized native Windows package/install/run workflow with its required original inputs kept separate; frozen component kits or cross-builds do not establish product packaging.

items.label: End-to-end native game acceptance
items.criterion: Accept a defined representative native game journey with the integrated IDE and required product behavior; component tests, emulator research and boot alone are insufficient.
items.evidence_class: No playable game or full-application acceptance
